label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is a False Positive because user input from InputStream is HTML-encoded via ESAPI.encodeForHTML before being written to the response, neutralizing the XSS vector. Alert 2 (java/http-response-splitting) is a True Positive because the user-supplied InputStream data flows directly into the Cookie header value ('SomeCookie') without sanitization of Carriage Return/Line Feed characters, enabling response splitting. Alert 3 (java/insecure-cookie) is triggered by the hardcoded setSecure(false), but the case is classified as TP due to the confirmed vulnerability in Alert 2.

evidence.note: User input from InputStream is read into str without CRLF filtering before being used in Cookie.
Cookie value str is added to response without sanitization, confirming response splitting risk.
XSS sink is mitigated by ESAPI.encodeForHTML(str) call prior to output.
